source.note: Criterion titles and weights are official. Acceptance evidence is an internal proof standard and is not presented as additional organizer scoring guidance.

criteria.title: Problem Identification
acceptanceEvidence: The presentation identifies the target user, validated pain point, urgency, and bounded problem scope.
Every external problem or urgency claim is traceable to a source.

criteria.title: Solution Alignment
acceptanceEvidence: The presentation connects each core feature to the stated problem and Tech for Good sub-theme.
The live product path demonstrates the claimed differentiating loop without unsupported capability claims.

criteria.title: Innovation & Uniqueness
acceptanceEvidence: The presentation explains why rubric-first, cited-evidence rehearsal differs from generic speaking feedback.
The demonstration shows unique product logic rather than only naming it.

criteria.title: Technical Execution
acceptanceEvidence: pnpm check passes on the submission state.
The deck explains the real tech stack, data flow, evidence validation, and deterministic fallback.
The full judge path works online and with network access disabled.

criteria.title: Design & User Experience
acceptanceEvidence: The full judge path passes desktop and 390px browser checks without overflow or console errors.
Evidence citations are visually prominent and all critical states remain readable on the real demo display.

criteria.title: Pitching and Q&A Response
acceptanceEvidence: Three consecutive rehearsals finish between 6:15 and 6:45 before the 7-minute hard stop.
The deck covers the required and recommended content, contains the live product and public repository links, and has a rehearsed operator handoff.
The Q&A bank contains at least 20 concise, evidence-supported answers and every mentor question.

criteria.title: Booth & Visual Display
acceptanceEvidence: The booth communicates the product's main idea and value without a verbal explanation.
The display, one-pager, official identity, and public-product QR are legible and tested on-site.

criteria.title: Interactive Demo & Prototype
acceptanceEvidence: A visitor can open the public product and complete the differentiating loop on their own phone.
Kiosk reset, semantic failure fallback, mobile layout, reload persistence, and offline operation are demonstrated.

criteria.title: Communication & Engagement
acceptanceEvidence: Booth staff can explain the problem, product loop, evidence citation, limitation, and next step concisely.
The staffing plan keeps visitors supported while at least 50% of the team attends the Innovation Forum.

criteria.title: Product Impact & Innovation
acceptanceEvidence: Booth materials connect the validated problem to product impact and a bounded future roadmap.
The live interaction makes the rubric-grounded innovation observable rather than relying on a claim.

requirements.requirement: Submit through Google Classroom by Thursday, 13 August 2026 at 18.00 WIB.
Submit the presentation deck as PDF or PPTX.
The cover states the team name, member names, product name, and logo.
The official RISTEK Hackathon 2026 logo is on the cover.
The deck includes a direct link to the final product.
The deck includes a public, accessible GitHub repository link.
The team arrives on schedule and brings its own display and demo devices.
At least 50% of the team attends the Innovation Forum while remaining members staff the booth.
On-site participants attend the entire event and notify the committee before leaving.
Every participant complies with the formal dress code.
The team rehearses the 2-minute preparation, 7-minute presentation, and 3-minute Q&A allocation.
The presentation has a rehearsed hard stop when the committee timer expires.
The submitted deck and operator handoff are tested without relying on presenter screen sharing.
The submission contains no plagiarism, fabricated data or sources, prohibited third-party involvement, or academic misconduct.
The team arrival plan targets 06.30 on 14 August 2026 and booth preparation from 07.30.
The staffing plan covers the 09.00–11.00 Innovation Forum and 09.00–12.00 exhibition visit.
The exact required submission file naming format is confirmed with Google Classroom or the team manager.
The organizer's AI-assistance interpretation is confirmed and the team's disclosure is accurate.
